subjects.displayTitle: Guarding the Covenant: separation and restraint
subjects.introduction: Avoid him, yet be not aggressive: ‘Abdu’l-Bahá’s counsel on those who break the Covenant binds two commands together that are easy to pull apart. The friends are to keep apart from anyone who sows doubt and division, to treat association as poison; and in the same breath they are forbidden to molest, censure, slander or confront, told to leave such a person in the hand of God and to deal with everyone in the most excellent manner. Behind the severe images of plague and leprosy lies a concern for protection rather than punishment, and alongside them run quieter instructions: investigate before judging, act with tact, never argue, and remember that sincere repentance, not merely words, reopens the door. Second Thessalonians asks a community to withhold company from one who disregards its instruction while still admonishing him as a brother, not an enemy [1]. The road onward leads into the nature of Covenant-breaking itself and into the wider question of fellowship with the wayward.
subjects.arc: Begin with the limits placed on hostile conduct, examine the concern for communal protection, and close with sincerity, repentance, and trust in God.

order.why: Open with vigilance explicitly bounded by nonaggression and freedom from slander.
shortened: O ye beloved ones, guard the Cause of God! Let no sweetness of tongue beguile you -- nay, rather consider the motive of every soul, and ponder the thought he cherisheth. Be ye straightway mindful and on your guard. Avoid him, yet be not aggressive! Refrain from censure and from slander, and leave him in the Hand of God.

order.why: Make the prohibition on harassment unmistakable.
shortened: Verily, enjoin upon the loved ones of God to refrain from molesting that deluded person. A stern prohibition! In truth I say: if any soul molests him, he was not and is not reckoned as being of the Truth - and God suffices as a witness.

order.why: Define moderation through abstaining from conflict and disputation.
shortened: The intention of moderation is that you should not engage in conflict and disputation, but also do not associate with them. Leave them to themselves.

order.why: Read leaving people alone beside excellent conduct.
Consider the instruction not to confront opponents.
shortened: You must greatly advise and counsel the friends lest anyone confront these people. The Arab poet said: "If I were to throw a stone at every barking dog, stones would become worth a dinar." Leave them in their vain pursuits.

order.why: Introduce tact rather than agitation.
shortened: Be not agitated by the clamour of the Yahya'is and others. These affairs are like unto the foam upon the sea: they come and they pass away. As for the Yahya'is, it is in no wise suitable that they should be present in your gatherings, for their sole aim is to cast doubts. Behave, then, with such tact and wisdom that they themselves will refrain from coming.

order.why: Notice the reported requirement to inquire into a doubtful situation.
Keep sincere repentance and forgiveness within view.
shortened: Therefore, the company of these people should be shunned and none should associate with them, unless they repent unto God. My Lord is verily the Compassionate, the Forgiving. Such repentance, however, must be sincere and not merely in words.

order.why: Identify the stated acts of division and distortion.
shortened: However, from those souls who cast doubts and seek to breach God's impregnable fortress, who wish to uproot the foundation of God's religion from its base, who distort the Book, and who break God's Covenant and Testament - from such souls one must absolutely keep distant and avoid, for the foul odor of Covenant-breaking is so putrid that even if it does not have an intense effect, it will inevitably distress the nostrils and cause weakness, laxity and feebleness.

order.why: Read the reported warning about deceptive appearances.
shortened: And so from the very beginning any such deviation must be prevented.

Of course, anyone who wants to gain a following and create division among the friends will at first resort to one of the divine verses and make himself appear to be sincere and deeply attached to the Faith. Words of humility and sacrifice flow from his tongue so that he may deceive the simple and the naive.

order.why: Examine the several forms that the passage attributes to deception.
shortened: Make every effort to protect them, for the people of doubts have arisen with various means - sometimes showing themselves as oppressed, sometimes uttering words of unity, sometimes praising the Intended One, sometimes claiming firmness and steadfastness by pen and tongue, so that through various deceptions they may cause wavering in the hearts of the steadfast ones.

order.why: Focus on vigilance against calumny and insinuation.
shortened: Therefore the honored Afnans of the Blessed Tree must always be alert and vigilant that this faction does not create damage through their calumnies, doubts and insinuations.

order.why: Read the warning against substituting imaginings for the revealed text.
shortened: Preserve the people from the whisperings of those who have seized upon vain imaginings and cast behind their backs what was revealed in My Preserved Tablet.

order.why: Compare a claim to faith with the conduct attributed to its claimants.
shortened: Say: O loved ones of God! Shun ye those who claim faith and attribute themselves to God while committing that which causeth all things to lament and the limbs of all names to tremble.

order.why: Consider the contrast drawn between strengthening and undermining the Covenant.
shortened: Should anyone come to you secretly and call you to waver in the Covenant and Testament, be not shaken; know that such a one is an evil person and among the companions of Satan. You must surely avoid him. Whosoever calls you to the divine Covenant is among the companions of the All-Merciful, and whosoever wavers is an enemy of the Blessed Beauty.

order.why: Read the warning that a document alone may not establish present faithfulness.
shortened: You must surely avoid these hate-filled souls who strive to destroy the edifice of the Abha Beauty and break the Covenant of that Peerless Beloved, even if they possess papers from 'Abdu'l-Baha in their hands. For the Covenant-breakers have a strong foul odor - avoid them as soon as you detect it.

order.why: Retain the account of Kheiralla and Abdu’l-Baha’s stated station.
shortened: There are letters preserved with the handwriting of Keirullah in which he clearly writes: 'I testify that thou art the Christ, the son of God;' but I did not accept this from him and wrote back that I am Abdul Baha. Now on account of some interest he is following the Nakezeens, but this interest will not remain, it will disappear. This century will pass and in the next century there will remain not one Nakez.

order.why: Locate the command within the history of the Bab’s Covenant.
Read the reported distinction concerning antagonistic association.
Consider the passage’s explanation of fellowship with religions.
shortened: It is necessary for the believing souls to associate with the righteous that thus they might inhale Holy Breaths. When He (Baha'u'llah) says, associate with all religions with joy and fragrance, by this is meant the human kind and not the wicked.

order.why: Hear the specific warning about repeated association.
Join withdrawal with trust in God.
shortened: Whosoever from whom they detect the fragrance of hatred, they must leave to himself and place their trust in God, exalted be His glory.

order.why: Read the call to seek a protected refuge.
Consider the difficult instruction concerning a brother or sister.
shortened: O My servants! Should any one of you hear that his brother or sister hath turned away from God, it behooveth him to turn away from that one and to turn towards the Beloved of the sincere ones.

order.why: Keep separation beside recourse to mercy.
shortened: Cleanse thou yourself from the love of these people, turn not thy face to them and befriend them not even for less than an instant. Avoid the likes of them and cling to the mercy of God and His generosity.

order.why: Hear the concise instruction to refrain from association.
shortened: Guard it from the manifestations of Satan who bid people to deny Him Who created them by His command, and who have taken for themselves a partner with God. Shun such as these, neither sit with them nor associate with them.

order.why: Read the movement from withdrawal toward God.
Continue the image of shelter under divine protection.
shortened: Beware lest thou sit with Mine enemies. Flee from them and shun them. Then take for thyself a station beneath the shadow of thy Lord's protection, which God hath purified from the doubts of time.

order.why: Consider steadfastness within the prohibition on association.
Retain the breadth of the instruction in the Prisoner’s address.
shortened: Say: O My loved ones and My chosen ones! Hearken unto the call of this Prisoner Who is confined in this Most Great Prison. Should you find anyone who showeth the least sign of aversion, turn away from him and eschew his fellowship. This is what We have enjoined upon you in all the Tablets, and to this do all things bear witness, both from the unseen realm and from the visible world, and beyond them the Beauty of matchless glory.

order.why: Connect turning away with continuing remembrance.
Read the contrasting bird images as polemical language.
shortened: Never can the cooing of the Dove be mistaken for the croaking of the raven of hatred, nor can the melodies of the birds of holiness be confused with the cries of crows and magpies. The screech of the falcon soaring in the heights of glory can never resemble the screeching and moaning of the owls of oppression. The glorification and praise of the Supreme Concourse can never accord with the ranting of the rabble in the lowest depths.

order.why: Retain the severe serpent image without adopting it as a description of human worth.
Read poison as the passage’s metaphor for influence.
shortened: Doctor Fareed, his mother and relatives intend to make a journey to those parts. These people are violators of the Covenant and in the utmost rebellion. Beware! Beware! Lest anyone associate with them. Association with them is poison. Warn all the friends.

order.why: Examine the extended sea and disease imagery in its historical argument.
shortened: These doubts of the Covenant-breakers are like the foam of the sea, and the sea cannot be without foam. The sea of the Covenant will surge once and cast out the dead bodies to the shore, for the sea does not accept dead bodies.
In brief, this foam of the sea has no permanence and will soon vanish and disappear, while the sea of the Covenant will surge eternally and remain in turmoil and upheaval.

One must associate with souls who are firm in the Covenant and befriend the righteous, for evil companions cause evil qualities to spread, like leprosy - it is impossible for one to associate with a leper and not contract leprosy. This is for protection and preservation.

order.why: Retain the cablegram’s scriptural and disease comparisons.
Keep the related medical metaphor in its source setting.
Read the physician image and the concern about publications.
shortened: In any case, you must exercise the utmost care lest the utterances or publications of these veiled ones influence the weak ones, or cloud the pure hearts of the simple ones, or their cold breath make the thoughtless ones grow cold. For doubts at all times act as a deadly poison which makes a healthy body sick or even destroys it. Therefore you must, holding fast to the Covenant like a kind physician, prevent this swift poison and treat this chronic and severe illness.

order.why: Consider the secure city as an image of protection.
shortened: We called it a secure city so that it might remain protected and safeguarded from the arrows of doubt of the Covenant-breakers.
Therefore, we beseech God to preserve and protect the nostrils of holy souls from this foul odor, which is like a deadly poison.

order.why: Retain the severe warning about an appearance of scriptural allegiance.
shortened: Be thou steadfast in the love of thy Lord, then detach thyself from the idolaters. And shouldst thou see the Satan from whom thou perceivest the stench of misbelief, shun him and be under mighty protection. He appears in human form and speaks of what was revealed in the Bayan, that he might cause confusion among Our weak servants.

order.why: Read the cawing image alongside trust in God.
shortened: Should a cawing one come unto thee, shun him and put thy trust in God, the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Continue the call to guard a station.
shortened: Guard this station through the Name of the Lord of Names, for the cawing ones have been and are lying in ambush.

order.why: Keep the particular account concerning Cyprus distinct.
Read the answer to accusations of political sympathy.
shortened: As to the matter of our ill-wishers amongst the Yahya'is [i.e. the Azalis], who accuse the Friends [i.e. the Baha'is] of sympathy with the Court [or Government, Dawlat], it is certain that the truth of the case will become plain and evident, and you should peruse the letters sent by this post to Mirza 'Abdu'llah Sahib-furush.

order.why: Locate the signed-document instruction within its historical travel setting.
Read the related conditions for admission to gatherings.
shortened: Be very mindful of this. Do not allow these souls into your gatherings and meetings. Associate only with one who has in hand a letter of permission with the writing and signature of 'Abdu'l-Baha. Otherwise avoid them and make excuses. No individual among you is permitted to associate with them, for spiritual diseases are like physical diseases - like plague and cholera and cancer they are contagious.

order.why: Retain the further travel instruction in that context.
shortened: Therefore He cabled and wrote to America, even to you, that if any Persian, whether stranger or acquaintance, should come to America without bearing in his hand a permit written and signed by Me, beware, beware of drawing nigh unto him. Not only must you not draw nigh to such a person, but do not even look at him.

order.why: Consider the reported response of the San Francisco community.
shortened: The friends in San Francisco are exceedingly firm. They do not receive violators in their homes. Recently a violator went to that city. The Baha'i friends turned him away, saying, "You are not with us; why do you try to come among us?"

order.why: Read the further instruction concerning association in its own context.
shortened: Do not allow these souls near you, avoid them completely. Until you are certain someone is completely detached from these corrupt ones, do not converse with them at all, for those parties are ill-intentioned and utterly corrupt, and prejudiced and unfair people.

order.why: Follow the instruction’s communication to American cities.
shortened: And whoever directs you to associate with them under any pretext, absolutely do not accept it, even if they praise them highly. And write this matter to each of the cities of America one by one, so they can announce it among the friends.

order.why: Read the specific warning involving Azal.
shortened: And when you observe that they make mention of Azal, at that time announce to all the friends that no one should go near them. These souls are very deceitful and full of tricks.

order.why: Consider the call to strengthen hearts.
shortened: You must strive night and day to strengthen hearts, and if you detect even the slightest whiff of wavering from any passerby, you must prevent the friends from associating with them.

order.why: Retain the emphatic warning and notice to the friends.
shortened: Most certainly, one hundred times certainly, if you detect the slightest whiff of that word which I am ashamed to mention and from which I seek refuge in God, you must completely avoid that person. The Blessed Beauty is disgusted with such a person, the Exalted One stands apart, and such a one is a bloodthirsty enemy to 'Abdu'l-Baha. Inform all the friends so they may be on their guard.

order.why: Sets out the injunction to avoid Covenant-breakers in relation to preserving the Cause.
Read the dated cablegram in its own setting.
Keep the second dated cablegram distinct.
Preserve the named-person instruction without generalizing it.
Read the related concise prohibition.
Consider the reported concern about gaining confidence before sowing division.
Read the account of attempted counsel and its outcome.
shortened: Mirza Asadu'llah went to London to counsel his son and wife and bring them to repentance, but it is clear that he joined them. His purpose too is to cast doubts. And regarding Sprague, it is as thou hast written - through subtle means she casts doubts, but in the end she will regret it.

order.why: Keep the reported warning beside the instruction never to argue.
shortened: He spoke of Farid and said, "Never argue with anyone," and then added:

If a Judas-like person should sell Christ and seek to destroy the very foundation of the Cause, is it meet that we should aid him? Or if a thief should desire to break into a house, should we assist him? Judas sold Christ for thirty pieces of silver; Dr. Farid sold us for four or five dollars. This foundation hath been reared through the blood of holy souls.

order.why: Retain the reported description of recognition in its own voice.
Examine the decision concerning a published response.
shortened: With this consideration those responses were recorded but not published. Now it is observed that this has become cause for their audacity. We are perplexed as to what course to take. In any case, the Glad Tidings treatise has now been published and thou hast sent it abroad. The person in question has written a rebuttal. Publish also the response to his rebuttal, that they might become mindful, though this is difficult, for understanding, recognition and feeling have vanished from this group, and they have become the manifestation of "What aileth these people that they fail to understand a single word?"

order.why: Read the instruction not to circulate a person’s name.
shortened: In any case wisdom is very necessary. Such persons should never be mentioned to anyone.

order.why: Consider leaving opponents to their own course.
shortened: Leave them in their stupefaction, bewildered.

And thou, O thou who art enkindled with the fire ignited in the heart of the world, leave aside the nations and the doubts of the weak ones in knowledge and judgment - the dull-witted, foolish, ignorant ones - regarding the power of the Covenant of the Ancient Beauty.

order.why: Retain the image of dependence even amid opposition.
shortened: Otherwise the matter will become so confused that those very birds of night that have been stirred to action will become nonexistent and rejected, for even the life of bats depends on the grace of the sun's heat.

order.why: Distinguish descendants from the course of their forebears.
shortened: I declare by the Educator of the visible and invisible, it will evidently be witnessed that the descendants of the violators will think their descent as a disgrace and will disown their fathers and forefathers, just as Akrama, the son of Abudjahl, kept clear of his father, and Kaled, the son of Valid, left his father.

order.why: Consider the reported difference between declared and sincere repentance.
shortened: Ahmad came and brought them all in. never associate with Mrs. Kirchner. Never speak a word to Mrs. Kirchner. When I was in Chicago she begged My pardon. I accepted her. At that very moment I realized she was lying. I made her understand that her repentance was not sincere. But using that pardon as a pretext she came and sewed seeds of intrigue.

order.why: Return to gratitude for a secure spiritual home.
shortened: Day and night engage in thanksgiving to the Forgiving Lord that you have taken up residence in this flourishing house and have become entirely detached from and averse to that buried foundation.

order.why: Close with prayer and the appeal to the Most Great Name.
shortened: I beseech Thee by the Most Great Name, through which the limbs of the idolaters trembled and the hearts of the deceivers were agitated - they who turned away from Thee and violated Thy Covenant and Testament, and followed their own desires in Thy days.

questions: How do the prohibitions on aggression, slander, and harassment shape your reading of the commands to keep apart?
What kinds of conduct and intention are described as threatening the Covenant, and what further context would be needed before applying a historical instruction?
How might the passages about inquiry, tact, and leaving people to themselves guide a response when trust is damaged?
What is gained, and what could be misunderstood, when spiritual conflict is described through medical or animal metaphors?
How does the comparison from Second Thessalonians illuminate the relationship between communal boundaries and the treatment of a person?
What questions about repentance, sincerity, and restoration arise from reading the promise of forgiveness beside the reported cases?

references.label: 1 · 2 Thessalonians 3:14–15 · Separation without treating a person as an enemy
references.note: In the King James Version, the letter directs the community to withhold company from someone who disregards its instruction, while still admonishing that person as a brother rather than treating him as an enemy. Compare this pairing of discipline and restraint with the compilation’s prohibitions on aggression and harassment. The two texts concern different communities and circumstances; the comparison does not make their rules interchangeable.

subjects.displayTitle: The fruit of creation: dignity that calls for a response
subjects.introduction: A tree exists for its fruit, and ‘Abdu’l-Bahá says plainly what the fruit of the human tree is: love, together with the inner and outer perfections that love brings to ripeness. To call humanity the fruit of creation is not a boast about rank. The fruit hangs on branches it did not grow, drinks from roots it cannot see, and its sweetness depends on the health of the whole tree, which is why the same teaching that names us the sum of all things asks us to sustain one another and to do some kindly thing each day for a fellow creature. Within a single person the mineral’s being, the plant’s growth and the animal’s senses are gathered up and crowned with a mind that can pierce to the reality of things and a heart able to reflect every name of God. The Qur’án speaks in a kindred voice of the children of Adam honoured, carried over land and sea, and provided with good things [1], a gift that quietly becomes a responsibility. The inquiry widens from here into what sets a human being apart from the animal, into the long story of evolution, and into the old insight that the human reality is a small world holding the great one within it; and it narrows, finally, to the Perfect Man in whom all this capacity is fully realised.
subjects.arc: Begin with shared dependence and love, explore the capacities gathered in humanity, and distinguish human potential from its fullest spiritual realization.

order.why: Read the potential reflection of divine names and attributes.
shortened: How resplendent the luminaries of knowledge that shine in an atom, and how vast the oceans of wisdom that surge within a drop! To a supreme degree is this true of man, who, among all created things, hath been invested with the robe of such gifts, and hath been singled out for the glory of such distinction. For in him are potentially revealed all the attributes and names of God to a degree that no other created being hath excelled or surpassed.

order.why: Open with all people sustained by one interdependent tree.
shortened: The Blessed Beauty saith: "Ye are all the fruits of one tree, the leaves of one branch." Thus hath He likened this world of being to a single tree, and all its peoples to the leaves thereof, and the blossoms and fruits. It is needful for the bough to blossom, and leaf and fruit to flourish, and upon the interconnection of all parts of the world-tree, dependeth the flourishing of leaf and blossom, and the sweetness of the fruit.

For this reason must all human beings powerfully sustain one another and seek for everlasting life; and for this reason must the lovers of God in this contingent world become the mercies and the blessings sent forth by that clement King of the seen and unseen realms.

order.why: Name love as the fruit to be produced.
shortened: The true fruit of man is therefore Love. The purpose of a tee is to produce fruit. Man is like a tree. His fruit should be Love.

order.why: Make inward and outward perfections a task.
shortened: Strive diligently to acquire both outward and inward perfections, for the fruit of the human tree has ever been outer and inner perfections.

order.why: Introduce intellect and wisdom as gifts with creative consequences.
Connect human distinction with knowing and loving God.
shortened: Having created the world and all that liveth and moveth therein, He, through the direct operation of His unconstrained and sovereign Will, chose to confer upon man the unique distinction and capacity to know Him and to love Him -- a capacity that must needs be regarded as the generating impulse and the primary purpose underlying the whole of creation, as mentioned in the well-known sacred tradition.

Upon the inmost reality of each and every created thing He hath shed the light of one of His names, and made it a recipient of the glory of one of His attributes. Upon the reality of man, however, He hath focused the radiance of all of His names and attributes, and made it a mirror of His own Self. Alone of all created things man hath been singled out for so great a favor, so enduring a bounty.

order.why: Consider planes and states hidden within a person.
shortened: 70 Likewise, reflect upon the perfection of man's creation, and that all these planes and states are folded up and hidden away within him.

order.why: Explore the diversity of qualities manifested in individuals.
Read humanity’s distinction as a gift of loving-kindness.
Answer the gift with gratitude.
shortened: All that has been created is for man who is at the apex of creation and who must be thankful for the divine bestowals, so that through his gratitude he may learn to understand life as a divine benefit.

order.why: Identify the acquisition of virtues as a purpose.
Gather existence, growth, and sensation in the human being.
Follow these capacities toward perception of realities.
shortened: Of all things in the world, man is the highest. Compare him with the mineral, the vegetable, and the animal.
But man, while possessing all the qualities and capacities of these three kingdoms, has besides them a perceiving power by which he may penetrate to the reality of all things.

order.why: Consider the knowledge of the kingdoms contained within humanity.
shortened: The noblest of all earthly beings is man. In him are realized the animal, the vegetable and the mineral kingdoms, that is, all these degrees are contained in him in such wise that he is endowed with them all. And, being endowed with all these degrees and stations, he is informed of their mysteries and aware of the secrets of their existence.

order.why: Explains humanity’s comprehensiveness through the perfections of the lower kingdoms.
Read the public address on combined perfections.
shortened: The Essence of Divinity, the Sun of Truth, shines forth upon all horizons and is spreading its rays upon all things. Each thing has some portion of that bounty, but the human reality, which combines the perfections of the mineral, the vegetable and animal, and as an additional token of grace, possesses the human perfections, is the noblest of created beings.

order.why: Keep the related public address in its own wording.
shortened: Each kingdom of creation is endowed with its necessary complement of attributes and powers. The mineral possesses inherent virtues of its own kingdom in the scale of existence. The vegetable possesses the qualities of the mineral plus an augmentative virtue, or power of growth. The animal is endowed with the virtues of both the mineral and vegetable plane plus the power of intellect. The human kingdom is replete with the perfections of all the kingdoms below it with the addition of powers peculiar to man alone. Man is, therefore, superior to all the creatures below him, the loftiest and most glorious being of creation.

order.why: Distinguish consciousness in the account of human capacities.
Read the reported comparison concerning thought.
Distinguish bodily attributes from spirit.
shortened: Man is not human by virtue of his body; man is human by virtue of his spirit. For in physical matters, man shares attributes with animals, but through the spirit he is distinguished from them.

order.why: Consider understanding illumined by spirit.
Explore knowledge as participation in humanity’s accumulated discoveries.
shortened: The greatest of human virtues is knowledge. Knowledge is the cause of divine bounty's manifestation. Knowledge is the discoverer of mysteries. Knowledge is like a mirror in which the images of all things are reflected. Knowledge gives to each person the learning of all humanity, and makes each individual human being equivalent to all humanity, because knowledge teaches one whatever all humanity has discovered - that is, whatever is known by all humanity.

order.why: Add conscious attraction to the account of love.
shortened: Finally, we reach the kingdom of man. Here we find that all the degrees of the mineral, vegetable and animal expressions of love are present plus unmistakable attractions of consciousness.

order.why: Locate humanity at a threshold between material and spiritual conditions.
shortened: Man is the most distinguished species in that he combines the perfections of all three classes--that is, he possesses a material body, the power of growth, and the power of sensation. Beyond the mineral, vegetable and animal perfections, however, he also possesses a special perfection of which other created things are bereft, namely, the perfections of the mind. Thus man is the noblest of all existing things.

Man is in the ultimate degree of materiality and the beginning of spirituality, that is, he is at the end of imperfection and the beginning of perfection. He is at the furthermost degree of darkness and the beginning of the light.

order.why: Hear the address on the importance of spirit.
Examine the root-and-branch argument about consciousness.
Consider the appearance of spiritual perfections in the world.
shortened: It is through the appearance of the spirit in the material body that this world is illumined. Just as the spirit of man is the cause of the life of his body, so is the whole world even as a body and man as its spirit. If man did not exist, if the perfections of the spirit were not manifested and the light of the mind was not shining in this world, it would be like a body without a spirit.

order.why: Read the world-body and human-spirit analogy.
shortened: The world of existence holds the station of one temple, one body; and man in comparison thereto is the spirit of such body. Just as the body, without spirit, is dead; even so the world of the existence minus the presence of man is as dead.
Were man absent in the world, the body of the world would be dead.

order.why: Notice the explicit distinction between physical presence and human attainments.
Return to the image of a tree requiring fruit.
shortened: For the enlightenment of the world dependeth upon the existence of man. If man did not exist in this world, it would have been like a tree without fruit.

order.why: Hear the concise tree analogy.
Consider the gardener’s purpose in planting.
shortened: The phenomena of the world are like unto the tree and man is similar unto the fruit thereof. The tree is planted, reared and watered for the sake of its fruits. If the gardener did not have the fruit as his ultimate object he would not have planted the tree.

order.why: Keep the report’s own identification of its language as examples and parables.
Explore a fruit’s hidden potential before its appearance.
shortened: Similarly, observe the weakness of the fruit's existence in the original tree before emerging from it - though within the tree it is so weak as to be completely imperceptible, such that if one were to cut the tree into pieces, not a trace of the fruit or its form would be found. Yet after emerging from the tree it appears with wondrous beauty and mighty strength, as can be observed in fruits, some of which become more delectable after being separated from the tree.

order.why: Distinguish later emergence from derivation in the fruit analogy.
Read development in body, knowledge, morals, and civilization.
Retain the historical argument about forms without presenting it as current scientific evidence.
shortened: The specificity and essentiality of things are permanent and changeless; only within the limits of a particular species do progress and decline occur. For example, the human species and human nature have been and will forever remain preserved and protected. As can be observed, the mummified ancient human bodies that have been extracted from the pyramids of Egypt, though five thousand years have passed since their death, have not changed or altered even by a hair's breadth from the human form.
There is no altering in God's creation.

order.why: Consider the claim of enduring human reality in its own terms.
shortened: O seeker of truth! Man is the greatest part of the world of existence and the fruit of the tree of the visible world. His species is eternal, and this everlasting reality has neither beginning nor end. What Western philosophers say about human evolution - that man has come from the mineral, vegetable and animal kingdoms and reached this station through growth and development - is mere fancy, for the human species is ancient. Perhaps on this earth it was initially like a seed, then progressed and reached the station of "the best of creators." But that seed which gradually developed was the human species, not animal. Therefore this species is ancient and was originally the noblest of earthly creatures.

order.why: Notice that the argument specifies the complete human being.
shortened: We regard man as the chief member because, among all created things, he encompasses all the perfections of existence.
Now, what we mean by "man" is the complete human being, the foremost person in the world, who is the sum of all spiritual and material perfections, and who is like the sun among all created things.

order.why: Read the extended distinction concerning the Perfect Man and spiritual proofs.
shortened: Thus man is a perfect mirror facing the Sun of Truth and is the seat of its reflection. The splendour of all the divine perfections is manifest in the reality of man, and it is for this reason that he is the vicegerent and apostle of God. If man did not exist, the universe would be without result, for the purpose of existence is the revelation of the divine perfections.

This Man of whom we speak here is not just any man: that which we intend is the Perfect Man. For the noblest part of the tree, and the fundamental purpose of its existence, is the fruit. A tree without fruit is of no use.

order.why: Consider the Perfect Man in relation to the Word of God.
shortened: Man is the sum of Creation, and the Perfect Man is the expression of the complete thought of the Creator -- the Word of God.

order.why: Follow the report’s explicit qualification of the word man.
Read the comparison of perfection and imperfection in its attributed form.
shortened: When we come to the estate of man, we find his kingdom is vested with a divine superiority. Compared to the animal, his perfection or his imperfection is superior. In comparison with man the perfection of a flower is insignificant.

order.why: Hear the reported summary of creation’s culmination.
Examine the question of lasting purpose and the end of bodily life.
shortened: The consummation of this limitless universe with all its grandeur and glory hath been man himself, who in this world of being toileth and suffereth for a time, with divers ills and pains, and ultimately disintegrates, leaving no trace and no fruit after him. Were it so, there is no doubt that this infinite universe with all its perfections has ended in sham and delusion with no result, no fruit, no permanence and no effect.

order.why: Extend the fruit image across successive cycles.
Read the educational aspiration in the address to students.
shortened: If you attain to this supreme goal all the elements of the world of creation will be ready to serve you at your bidding, i.e. they will find their highest attainment in you and through you or, in other words, you will become the fruits of the world of existence... The evolution of the perfect man is a fruit of creation, just as the evolution of the trunk, branches, leaves and blossoms of the tree is the fruit thereof.

order.why: Consider freedom from darkness as the fruit of existence.
shortened: Regard this globe. Its divisions are mineral, vegetable and animal. Man is the result of all these; therefore man is the result of all existence here.

This is the fruit of the tree of creation - to be freed from the darkness of the planet in order to enter the worlds of light. This is the object of existence; this is the fruit of the tree of humanity.

order.why: Read the passage concerning the destiny of the true believer.
Keep the Bab’s warning about testimony and entrusted gifts within the complete selection.
Close the linked readings with every being receiving divine bounty.
shortened: Yet contingent being, in its existence and conditions, needs the outpouring from the Necessary Being. Thus the Impenetrable Unseen, transcendent beyond consciousness, has manifested to the realities of things through Names and Attributes. Nothing exists but has its portion of this divine outpouring and merciful manifestation, and "there is nothing but glorifies His praise."
As for man, he combines all contingent perfections - the mineral body, the vegetable refinement, the animal senses - and beyond these, he possesses divine perfection through grace.

order.why: Retain the supplied pilgrim-note version of the tree image.
Read the supplied account of Ibn Arabi as a distinct philosophical interpretation.
shortened: All beings other than Man only reflect, each one of them, singly, one aspect of the Absolute.

Man, on the contrary, not only synthesizes all the forms of the Divine self-manifestation which are scattered over the world of Being, but also is conscious of this whole. This is why a true comprehensive unity is established by Man, corresponding to the Unity of the Absolute. Man is in this sense the Imago Dei. And because of this peculiarity, Man can be ... the 'vicegerent' of God on the earth.

questions: How does the interdependence of fruit, branches, and tree affect the meaning of humanity’s distinction?
What becomes possible through the combination of growth, perception, thought, and love described in these passages?
Where does the text speak of human beings generally, and where does it specify the Perfect Man?
How can the tree and mirror images illuminate purpose while leaving room for careful scientific investigation of physical development?
What responsibilities might follow from the Qur’anic affirmation of honor and provision for the children of Adam?
If love is the fruit of human life, what would its cultivation and ripening look like in a community?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 17:70 · Honor bestowed on the children of Adam
references.note: Pickthall’s translation affirms that the children of Adam have been honored, carried on land and sea, provided with good things, and favored above many created beings. Compare the verse’s emphasis on bestowed dignity with the compilation’s accounts of human capacity and gratitude. Attend to the verse’s own wording and scope, and ask how a received gift might become a responsibility toward others.

subjects.displayTitle: The rejection of Muhammad: learning to recognize the light
subjects.introduction: Those who loved the lamp of Jesus, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá observed, failed to see the same light when it shone from another lamp in Arabia. The rejection of Muhammad is a story of stones thrown at a Prophet’s heel, of thirteen years of persecution in Mecca and a flight by night to Medina, and also a mirror held up to every believer. The nobles and divines turned away while a seller of dates believed; a Persian seeker and a shepherd recognised what the learned refused. The Writings press a disarming question about the proof by which people accepted Muhammad yet turned from the One who came after Him. The pattern is old: Matthew recounts how the people of Jesus’ own country, knowing his family, could not accept his wisdom [1]. Following this history honestly means asking whether familiarity has become a veil. It leads toward a deeper meeting with Muhammad and Islam, toward the heedlessness that blinds whole generations, and toward the rejection of Christ, whose sufferings tell the same story.
subjects.arc: Begin with the lamp and its light, hear the experience of rejection, and examine the expectations and standards that shape recognition.

order.why: Open with attachment to the lamp contrasted with love of its light.
shortened: When the Lights of prophethood shone forth from Mohammed, those who loved the Light believed in Mohammed, but those who loved the lantern of Jesus Christ refused to accept Mohammed. If we have a lamp lighted in the room tonight, and tomorrow we have another lamp, would we not be foolish not to accept the light, though the lamps are changed?

order.why: Question prestige through the believer who sold dates.
Ask whether the same standard of evidence is being applied consistently.
shortened: Were ye to be fair, by what proof did ye believe in Muhammad, the Apostle of God, and by what evidence did ye turn away from Him Who came to you with that which is with the All-Knowing?

order.why: Ground the inquiry in the account of persecution and migration.
Read the related account of danger to the early followers.
Keep the reported continuation of opposition in its setting.
Hear the lament over the suffering of the Messenger.
Read the detailed account of mockery, injury, and flight.
shortened: Yet in that time, all those people rose up to harm Him - they broke His blessed tooth and threw so many stones at His blessed heel that blood flowed, and they mocked and ridiculed Him in the streets and bazaars. In the blessed verse He relates: "When they see you, they treat you only with ridicule (saying): 'Is this the one whom God has sent as a Messenger?'" They threw dirt on His blessed head and scattered thorns in His path, and at night they would plot to shed His pure blood.
Things became so difficult for His Holiness in Mecca that He fled to Medina in the middle of the night from the hands of the enemies.

order.why: Consider the reported refuge sought in Abyssinia.
Contrast the wealth of opponents with the treatment described.
Notice the reported doubts even among outward companions.
Read the several forms of opposition named in the passage.
shortened: Say: O Siyyid, reflect upon Muhammad - may the spirit of all else be sacrificed for Him - and His manifestation in Yathrib and Batha. The humiliation that befell Him was first from the opposition of His relatives and kin, second from the opposition of the divines and mystics, third from the neglect of the people of the city and surroundings, and fourth - which was greatest of all - from the seven scholars who later ascribed many partners to Him, even while they considered themselves believers and the most excellent of all people.

order.why: Contrast Salman’s journey with opposition from relatives.
shortened: "In the days of His Holiness Muhammad, Salman came from Persia and believed in Him, but His own relatives rose against Him.

order.why: Return to humble believers and learned opponents.
Read the shepherd’s recognition beside scholarly refusal.
shortened: After His appearance from the horizon of Hijaz, all the divines of that age from among the Jews and Christians, despite their anticipation of His appearance, after His manifestation raised the standards of discord and arose in utter opposition. One who was among the most learned of divines remained deprived of the Sun of Truth, while one who was but a shepherd attained the knowledge of the Manifestation of the All-Merciful, and drank from the water of life.

order.why: Hear that contrast in a concise form.
shortened: Consider the time of the Apostle of God, that is, His Holiness the Seal - the divines were shut out while the shepherd attained.

order.why: Consider the narrowing of space through opposition.
shortened: The learned ones turned away from Him and the scholars objected, until the earth became strait for Him by Whom the horizons were illumined.

order.why: Keep early hostility beside later widespread acceptance.
shortened: In the early years, all the divines, men of letters and nobles united in complete opposition to shed His pure blood, yet after His Cause was exalted, a great multitude turned toward the divine horizon of revelation and the dawning-place of celestial light.

order.why: Read the warning about heedlessness.
shortened: Then remember when Muhammad, the Apostle of God, came, and how every heedless and doubtful one rose up against Him.

order.why: Identify imaginings as a barrier.
Read opposition in the language of the Covenant.
shortened: Remember when Muhammad, the Apostle of God, came, the people turned away from Him and those who violated God's Covenant and His Testament opposed Him, following every rebellious satan.

order.why: Places the rejection of Muhammad in the pattern of opposition to earlier Messengers.
Retain the passage concerning learned opponents.
Place the stated purpose of guidance beside the accusation of sorcery.
Distinguish denial, mockery, and condemnation.
shortened: Consider and call to mind the day on which Muhammad the Messenger of God appeared with the signs of God, the Help in Peril, the Self-Subsisting: some among the people denied Him, others turned away from Him, yet others mocked Him, and still others rose up against him in such grievous fashion as to sentence Him to death without any clear proof from God, the Lord of all being.
The more strenuously He admonished them, the greater waxed their enmity and hatred.

order.why: Hear the related account of escalating opposition.
Pause with the instruction to remember what befell Muhammad.
shortened: Look and remember what befell Muhammad, the Apostle of God, aforetime when He arose and called the people to God, the Lord of Lords.

order.why: Read Baha’u’llah’s lament for the Seal of the Prophets.
Continue the lament concerning later treatment.
Hear the accusation of madness as the adversaries’ words.
Keep the accusation of sorcery similarly attributed.
Consider the objection to an ordinary human messenger.
Compare the accusation with that directed toward Jesus.
Read ridicule within the scriptural pattern invoked.
Identify fabricated stories as a subject of criticism.
Consider the reported challenge to hostile accounts circulating in the West.
shortened: Much that is written or said about Moham[ad] is pure fabrication. The reality is not stated, because it is misunderstood. The origin of the current opinion held about his mission and character in the West is based upon false assumptions and prejudiced statements propagated by Christian authors and missionaries.

order.why: Read the concern about contempt and mockery in another setting.
Retain the historical defense without adopting its medical or cultural generalizations.
shortened: As for what European and American historians have written regarding Muhammad, the Messenger of God, most of it is slander.

Observe that that noble Person was born among ignorant nomads in the Arabian desert, associated and lived with them, and outwardly received no education and was devoid of reading and writing. Yet despite this, He established such a nation and laid down such a law, and made statements on scientific matters with supreme eloquence, and raised such a people from the depths of ignorance and savagery to the highest degree of civilization and prosperity, such that in Andalusia and Baghdad sciences, knowledge, arts and innovations made extraordinary progress in that age.

order.why: Hear the questions posed about missionary objections.
shortened: What are the objections of the Christian missionaries to the prophetic mission of Mohamad and with what evidences should they be contradicted? Why the eyes of other nations were veiled of the Mohamadic Beauty? Why did they not receive a portion and a share of the inexhaustible Bounties? Why were they deprived of the Celestial Bestowals?

order.why: Consider the accumulation of writings in opposition.
shortened: Verily, a thousand books were written by the sages and philosophers in rejection of Christ--may my spirit be a sacrifice unto Him--and even more were written against the Prophet, for there exist thousands of works by Christian and Jewish divines, all of which reject the Prophet--peace be upon Him--and still they are not content but continue to write.

order.why: Read the comparison of objections to miracles.
Keep the reported argument from military events within its historical voice.
Retain the broad reported comparison without making it a present description of communities.
shortened: The Christians have never praised so highly the Mohamadan religion nor a Jew has had a good word to say about Christ.

order.why: Hear the stated objection that an earlier revelation is sufficient.
Consider how scripture is invoked to support that objection.
Read the criticism of literal interpretation.
Compare misunderstandings of prophecy across dispensations.
shortened: Mohammed came according to the Gospels. As the Christians looked only to the literal meaning, they did not believe in Him. The believers of Christ were veiled from knowing Mohammed by the misunderstanding of the prophecies, just as the Jews were veiled from knowing Christ.

order.why: Examine the perceived conflict between scriptural texts.
Read the symbolic interpretation of the splitting moon and falling stars.
shortened: The splitting of the moon has multiple meanings and is not limited to its outward meaning. Among these meanings is the dissolution of those souls who, before the rising of the Sun of Oneness from the Muhammadan horizon, had illumined people with the lights of their sciences, wisdom and knowledge - like those souls who, in the Christian dispensation before the appearance of the Beauty of Ahmad, called people to the straight path and the mighty way, and from whose tongues shone forth the lights of knowledge and wisdom they had borrowed from the lamp of Jesus and the niche of Christ, and by whose guidance and direction and light of wisdom and knowledge people walked the path of guidance.

When the Most Great Light and the Ancient Sun appeared from the dawning-place of Yathrib and Batha, these souls did not succeed in believing and were not illumined by that Sun of the horizon of unity. Therefore these stars fell and the moon was split, as expressed in "When the sun arose, the moon was cleft."

order.why: Keep the reported interpretation of John within its own religious perspective.
shortened: In the New testament John 1:25 : Why baptizes thou then if thou be not that Christ nor Elias nor that Prophet. "That Prophet" signifies Mahomet - but Christians have not understood these references in their own Bible.

order.why: Read the Bab’s account of expectation and response.
Continue the contrast between a promise and its recognition.
Consider the Bab’s further appeal to remember earlier adversaries.
Read the parallel concerning Jesus and Muhammad.
Follow the comparison toward the influence of religious leadership.
shortened: Remember when Muhammad, the Apostle of God, came with clear signs, He was opposed by those possessed of learning, and before Him, when the Spirit came, the doctors of the Torah turned away from Him and the people followed them until God raised Him to an exalted station. Thus was the matter decreed aforetime. He, verily, is the All-Knowing, the All-Informed.

order.why: Hear the parallel account of accusations against Christ.
Consider mockery directed toward religious practices.
Read the preservation of the lamp amid attempts to extinguish it.
Turn from historical reflection to prayer for patience.
shortened: O God, unto Thee I complain of what hath befallen Islam, aforetime and hereafter. "Our Lord! Pour out patience upon us, and grant us victory over the company of the idolaters."

order.why: Read the warning addressed to learned people in a later setting.
Consider contention over religious names and titles.
Keep the passage about the Qa’im within the broader historical selection.
shortened: In these days it hath become clear and evident what manner of calumnies were spread in the past. The one who reported the existence of the Qa'im was a woman. When they asked the revered Ja'far whether the honored 'Askari had any male offspring, that wronged one refused and said that there had been a child two years before who had died.

order.why: Read the polemical reflection on expectation and the Bab’s martyrdom.
Confront the contrast between praying for an advent and opposing its appearance.
shortened: The former people denied the verses and showed ingratitude for the special bounty. They kindled the fire of tyranny and burnt the pavilion of the glory and grandeur of God's Cause and rent the veil of sanctity. Glory be to God! Night and day they would beseech and implore to attain the presence of the Self-Sufficient, the Most High. Yet when the dawn of grace broke and the world was illumined by the effulgences of the Daystar of Revelation, they all drew swords and spears against the Goal of the worlds. They were unbelievers yet counted themselves among the believers.

order.why: Read the extension of the pattern to the new revelation.
shortened: Say: The Day hath come and He Who conversed on Sinai speaketh: Verily there is no God but Him, the Truth, the Knower of the unseen. Behold, then mention what the people of the Furqan committed when the All-Merciful came with manifest sovereignty. The divines and doctors of the earth turned away from Him and pronounced judgment against Him with such injustice as caused the denizens of the Kingdom and the dwellers of the Realm of Might to lament.

order.why: Close with proclamation and suffering in Baha’u’llah’s own setting.

questions: What does the distinction between a lamp and its light reveal about religious loyalty and recognition?
How do the accounts of humble believers challenge assumptions about who is best placed to recognize truth?
What different roles do social familiarity, inherited interpretations, and hostile reports play in these selections?
How can a reader examine historical polemic without turning it into a judgment about whole religious communities today?
What does Matthew’s account of Jesus in his own country add to the question of familiarity and expectation?
How might the appeal to use a consistent standard of evidence change the way you investigate a claim outside your familiar tradition?

references.label: 1 · Matthew 13:54–58 · Familiarity and the refusal to recognize
references.note: In the King James Version, people hearing Jesus in his own country question the source of his wisdom by recalling his family and familiar place among them. Compare this response with the compilation’s accounts of expectations surrounding Muhammad. The comparison concerns a pattern of recognition and refusal; it need not erase differences between the histories or turn the passage into a prediction of another event.

subjects.displayTitle: The press: a mirror with responsibilities
subjects.introduction: Bahá’u’lláh called the newspaper a mirror of the world endowed with hearing, sight and speech, and then asked its writers to be purged of selfish passion, clothed in justice, and willing to enquire into a situation before setting it down. He addressed the papers of the cities directly, asking whether they had heard the moaning of the oppressed, and He lamented the sheets that print whatever anyone says because fresh news sells. ‘Abdu’l-Bahá makes the editor a moulder of public opinion, a champion of the poor, a remover of misunderstanding between races and religions, whose truthfulness lights the world like the sun and whose falsehood is never forgotten. Beside these principles stand the ordinary cares of running a journal: contributors, languages, subscriptions, and the occasional decision that a paper should not be founded at all. The Qur’an’s command to verify a report before harming people in ignorance states the same discipline in a sentence [1]. Readers as well as writers are drawn from here toward the review of publications and the power of the spoken and written word.
subjects.arc: Begin with hearing the oppressed, establish the discipline of truthful reporting, and explore how editorial purpose becomes practical publication work.

order.why: Introduce the mirror endowed with hearing, sight, and speech.
shortened: The pages of swiftly-appearing newspapers are indeed the mirror of the world. They reflect the deeds and the pursuits of divers peoples and kindreds. They both reflect them and make them known. They are a mirror endowed with hearing, sight and speech.

However, it behoveth the writers thereof to be purged from the promptings of evil passions and desires and to be attired with the raiment of justice and equity. They should enquire into situations as much as possible and ascertain the facts, then set them down in writing.

order.why: Open with the appeal to investigate the suffering of the oppressed.
shortened: O newspapers of the cities and lands! Have ye heard the moaning of the oppressed and their lamentations, or have these remained concealed from you? We hope that ye will investigate and proclaim that which hath occurred, that perchance your wise counsels and admonitions may awaken the heedless servants and adorn them with the ornament of justice.

order.why: Place that promise beside the danger of uninvestigated novelty.
shortened: Yet it is regrettable that some newspapers publish fabricated reports without investigation. Whatever anyone may say, they say, and whatever anyone may write, they write. Thus do the dawning-places of vain imaginings spread their fancies through newspapers.

The manifestations of vain imaginings send writings to newspapers day and night, and these are published without investigation. As some seek fresh news, they publish them. I beseech God to aid all to act according to His exalted Word: "Believe not every speaker, nor be assured by every arrival."

order.why: Make investigation before publication explicit.
shortened: The Editor of a newspaper or a Magazine must ever take the side of Truth. Every fact before its publication must be thoroughly investigated. An editor is the moulder of public opinions, the educator of the masses of mankind. Truth is his sharpest weapon. Forceful, strong statements his impregnable fort, and plain, direct language his shield.

order.why: Consider a concrete appeal to check documentary evidence.
Read the lasting consequences of truthful or false reporting.
Connect reporting with facts that later become apparent.
Contrast service to truth with selfish ends.
Explore the conditions of sincerity and justice.
Read the reported account of the press as protector of rights.
shortened: The Editors of the Newspapers are the guardians of the rights of man. They are the champions of the poor and the protectors of the Wronged ones. They are the crusaders after righteousness and moral purity. They are the advanced guards of the renaissance of education and arts and the pioneers of the higher development and spiritual unfoldment. They are the first and most effective instruments for establishing good relation and real understanding between the most remote nations of the world.

They must be the heralds of the oneness of the world and the teachers of true brotherhood. They must incite and encourage the people in the exercise of love, tolerance, chastity and good-fellowship and teach them to shun hatred and animosity.

order.why: Consider communication that removes misunderstanding among peoples.
Introduce journalists investigating conditions directly.
Read the reported example of a false victory announcement.
Return to the pressure to publish new stories without inquiry.
Recounts a seeker beginning an investigation after encountering the Cause in a newspaper.
Examine the choice not to answer every hostile report.
Keep the specific concern about hostile publications in context.
shortened: Your resolve is lofty and your aims are noble, for certain publications are being produced in Iran at the instigation of the Yahyais, and some are from the Yahyais themselves.

order.why: Read the attribution of rumors in another letter.
shortened: Observe in the Hablu'l-Matin newspaper that all these rumors are from the Yahyais.

order.why: Retain the description of press commotion in Egypt.
Hear the concise account of daily attention.
shortened: From every direction the people of this land are in search and discussing in gatherings. The newspapers raise a cry each day and write detailed articles. From sunrise until sunset and nightfall, even until midnight, there is a rush of seekers.

order.why: Read the report of widening newspaper coverage.
shortened: Today all the world's newspapers are occupied with mention of this Cause - there is no newspaper that has not mentioned and does not mention this Cause.
The copy of the article from the Petersburg newspaper was noted. Hereafter you will read many such newspapers.

order.why: Keep the reported comparison of coverage in its historical setting.
shortened: Today almost all the papers of the world are praising the Cause. The only papers which are scorning the Cause are those of our own country, that is Persia.

order.why: Consider the circulation of believers’ addresses.
shortened: Today the Press of the world belonging to various nations have taken the opportunity to publish the addresses of the believers of God and are printing them in their magazines.

order.why: Examine the decision to circulate an imperfect account.
Read the reported refusal of newspaper involvement beside the preceding encouragement.
Distinguish the conditions placed on a proposed magazine.
shortened: As for what you found favorable regarding the publication of a monthly magazine in Arabic and Persian to be distributed in various lands - wisdom does not require this at present unless it be purely scientific and literary, not containing a word of political articles or news.

order.why: Consider the selection of educational and nonpolitical letters.
Read the reported preference for broad principles over dogmatic assertion.
Connect a wider range of subjects with readers beyond the community.
shortened: "Likewise, great importance must be given to the development of the STAR OF THE WEST. The circle of its discussion must be widened; in its columns must be published the essential problems pertaining to the Bahai life in all its phases. Its contents must be so universal that even the strangers may subscribe to it.

order.why: Join attraction and happiness to factual accuracy.
Notice clarity of writing and the intentions attributed to its authors.
Read poetry and prose as vehicles for significant ideas.
Consider the purpose of beneficial articles.
Ask which subjects give a publication lasting value.
Compare timely reports with the image of enduring articles.
Return to the magazine as a mirror of truth.
Read the journal as a record of events and progress.
Consider the aspiration embodied in the title Sun of Truth.
Read the complete proposed opening for a journal, including its main statement.
shortened: At present thou hast started a journal. It is my hope that this journal will shine as the Star of the East. In the journal write thus:
When the horizon of the East was covered with immense darkness; when dark clouds were predominate, and when all the heavenly stars were concealed to the eye.

order.why: Consider publishing selections from the Treatise on Civilization.
Notice the request to preserve an address without abbreviation.
shortened: The address delivered in Stanford University and published completely in your paper was observed today--and on account of it I became both pleased and grateful.
After reading its contents should you think it best you may print it fully without abbreviation in the columns of your paper that others of the Jews may read it.

order.why: Read the account of passages omitted from an interview.
Consider translation and circulation of an article and report.
shortened: Have the newspaper article translated and printed together with a copy of the report, and disseminate them in other directions.

order.why: Follow the distribution of diary letters.
Read the request to inquire about and publish Tolstoy’s letter.
Consider efforts to place an article before a wider audience.
shortened: Endeavor thou that this Article may appear in the London Times. If this is impossible, i.e., its publication in the columns of the Times, then publish it by all means in other important periodicals or journals. This question along with this article is very important. Display ye the utmost effort in its publication.

order.why: Read the request to publish sayings in the Christian Commonwealth.
Consider the work of a correspondent and distributor.
shortened: O my heavenly friend! The letter which the editor of the Christian Commonwealth wrote to you was noted. It would be better if you were to be the correspondent of this journal and distribute its issues.

order.why: Hear appreciation for published articles.
Recognize the contribution of Jean Masson.
Read praise for an article in a St. Petersburg newspaper.
shortened: O well-wisher of the human world! The article that was published in the St. Petersburg newspaper was in the utmost eloquence and excellence, and it was evidence of your outstanding services.

order.why: Consider correspondence, languages, and revision arrangements.
shortened: Regarding the proposition which thou hast suggested that one of the maid-servants of the Merciful reside in the Land of Desire and be the medium for the regulation of correspondence, now it is not according to wisdom.
Therefore now edit thou a magazine in Persian and English, then forward it here to be revised and sent back for publication.

order.why: Recognize Gertrude Buikema’s service and bilingual publication.
shortened: Now the Star of the West should be written in both English and Persian. Miss Gertrude Buikema truly serves the Star of the West.

order.why: Join orderly management with communication between East and West.
Consider gradual improvement and access to educational letters.
Hear encouragement for publication and circulation.
Read the future hope addressed to an initially small journal.
shortened: Thou art the first Baha'i journal established in the American continent.

Although at present thy readers are few and thy volume small and thy voice weak, yet shouldst thou stand unshakable and become the object of the attention of the friends and the center of the generosity of the firm ones in the Covenant, in future thy readers shall embrace throngs upon throngs like waves of the sea, thy volume shall increase, thy arena shall become vast, thy voice and fame shall be raised and become world-wide and at last thou shalt become the first paper of the world.

order.why: Consider the material aftermath of wartime disruption.
Make the need to cover expenses explicit.
Read the appeal for financial support beyond one person’s means.
Hear the concise call to assist a library and magazine.
Consider promotion and the adequacy of contributions.
shortened: The Star of the West magazine has gained importance - you must certainly promote it among the friends. Its cost is small. Obtain and send it to America as this will lead to its promotion. According to what has been heard, so far only fifty tumans have been sent to America for the Star of the West newspaper. This amount is very small.

order.why: Read the concern about subscriptions and irregular appearance.
Follow the history of Chihrihnama’s circulation.
Consider service amid opposition to that journal.
shortened: In Shiraz some foolish and base individuals have spoken against you, but they were immediately disappointed and lost. This commotion and raving will cause Chihrihnama to reveal its face and this unique journal will gain great importance now and in the future. His honor Mirza Abdul-Hussein has truly rendered a great service to Chihrihnama.

order.why: Read the encouragement addressed to its editor.
shortened: To the respected editor of the unique newspaper Chihrihnama, may God strengthen him with hosts from on high.
In brief, everything proceeded according to your wishes and in these days Chihrihnama has brightened faces in some provinces.

order.why: Recognize persistence when other papers ceased publication.
Retain the recollection of early newspaper delivery.
shortened: In those days, the Tehran Gazette, the first Iranian newspaper, was brought to the Consulate once every month.

order.why: Examine the specific decision about republication and its possible benefit.
Close with the hope that a journal can enlighten hearts.
shortened: Convey my greetings, longing and respect to the editor of Labor Review and say that in future centuries your journal will surpass all the journals of the world, for you have announced the Kingdom of Abha, and I hope you will succeed in promoting the teachings of Baha'u'llah. Then you will observe that this journal has become a brilliant star and the cause of enlightenment of human hearts.

questions: What does the image of a speaking, seeing, hearing mirror reveal about the power and limits of journalism?
What practices of investigation are suggested by the passages on fabricated news and the request to check telegraph records?
How can reporting defend the wronged while remaining accurate and fair toward everyone involved?
What do the differing decisions about publication suggest about attending to purpose, audience, and circumstances?
How does the Qur’anic warning connect the verification of information with responsibility for its effects?
What habits could readers, editors, and contributors develop together to make public communication more trustworthy?

references.label: 1 · Qur’an 49:6 · Verify a report before causing harm
references.note: Pickthall’s translation instructs believers to verify tidings brought by an unreliable moral agent, lest they harm people in ignorance and later regret it. Compare that link between inquiry and consequences with the compilation’s demands on newspaper writers. The verse also opens a question for the receiver of news: what responsibility accompanies believing or passing on a report?

subjects.displayTitle: Praying for assistance: receiving strength to serve
subjects.introduction: Make my heart overflow with love for Thy creatures, ‘Abdu’l-Bahá prays, and let me become a sign of Thy mercy: the plea for help turns, almost at once, into a plea to be of help. Prayer for assistance in the Bahá’í writings carries every kind of need into the open. The weak one seeks the dayspring of power, the sick one the river of healing, a scattered and wounded people ask for a cure from the dispensary of mercy, a servant presses his brow into the dust at dawn and dusk while enemies scheme. Some petitions are urgent and exact; others, more searchingly, ask only for what is worthy, what is pleasing to God, what is best in this world and the next, leaving the measure of benefit in wiser hands. Many are offered for someone else, a friend, a leader, a household, a whole community. Moses, charged with a task beyond him, asked for an opened heart, clearer speech and his brother as companion, and the asking itself was the start of the work [1]. The journey continues toward God’s grace and bounty, His forgiveness, and the mercy that answers every supplicant.
subjects.arc: Begin with assistance that becomes service, give voice to need, and widen the prayer toward others and the refinement of desire.

order.why: Hear the collective prayer of wounded and scattered people.
shortened: O Lord! O Forgiving One! We are a group scattered and dispersed. We are Thine, and though we be strangers, yet are we Thy kindred. We are without head or refuge, helpless and remediless. We are wounded by every arrow, and cut by every sword. Bestow upon us a cure from the dispensary of Thy mercy, and grant us a healing balm from Thy supreme panacea, that these broken hearts may find solace, and these withered and dejected souls may find rest and gladness. May this night of sorrows be followed by a bright morn, and may this deadly poison be sweetened by wondrous honey.

order.why: Open with a request for the capacity to love and serve others.
shortened: Illumine my face with the radiance of the orb of Thy bounty, and graciously aid me in ministering at Thy holy threshold.

Make my heart overflow with love for Thy creatures and grant that I may become the sign of Thy mercy, the token of Thy grace, the promoter of concord amongst Thy loved ones, devoted unto Thee, uttering Thy commemoration and forgetful of self but ever mindful of what is Thine.

order.why: Give voice to weakness, illness, weariness, and poverty.
shortened: My God, my God! Thou seest the weak one seeking the dawning-place of Thy strength and the dayspring of Thy power, the sick one the Kawthar of Thy healing, the weary one the kingdom of Thy utterance, and the poor one the heaven of Thy wealth and bounty.

order.why: Read the appeal for a way forward and healing.
shortened: O God! Open Thou the way for this helpless one, grant Thou the remedy to this ailing one and bestow Thy healing upon this afflicted one. With burning heart and tearful eyes I supplicate Thee at Thy Threshold.

order.why: Consider refuge, joy, and a renewed portion of life.
shortened: Commune in prayer and say:

O Kind Lord! O Pure God! Grant this feeble servant a shelter beneath the shade of Thy Word of Mercifulness, and give this sorrowful one a refuge in the shadow of the Tree of Joy. Bestow a portion upon this portionless one, and confer a share upon this shareless one. From the ocean of Thy grace send forth a drop, and from the river of Thy bounty vouchsafe a sprinkling, that I may find fresh life and seek boundless favor.

order.why: Bring weakness beside the request for strength.
shortened: O Lord! I am weak - strengthen me in Thy Cause. I am poor - enrich me from the treasures of Thy Kingdom. I am lowly - aid me through the sovereignty of Thy might.

order.why: Read the transformation of fear into assurance.
Picture the weak one holding to the cord of power.
shortened: My Lord! Thou seest this weak one who hath clung to the cord of Thy power and raised his hands in supplication toward the heaven of Thy bounty and grace.

order.why: Keep the plea of helplessness and the request for protection together.
shortened: I beseech Thee, O Mystery of Being and O Thou in Whose grasp lie the reins of the seen and unseen, to aid me in that which befitteth Thy wondrous Cause and beseemeth Thy glorious Day. Then write down for me, through Thy bounty and favor, that which shall preserve me from the croaking which Thou hast foretold and from its transgression.
O my Lord! I am the helpless one, the wretched one, standing before the door of Thy mercy. I beseech Thee not to deny me [that which lieth with Thee].

order.why: Locate the prayer for strength amid oppression and danger.
Hear the request for another person’s protection.
shortened: O Lord! Aid him through Your merciful confirmations, assist him in all affairs, and protect him from every treacherous transgressor and frustrated envier.

order.why: Retain the prayer in its context of threatened opposition.
shortened: O my God! I press my brow and cover my face with the dust of lowliness, impotence and contrition, beseeching Thee at eventide and at dawn, supplicating before Thee in the darkness of night and the bright light of day, that Thou mayest assist Thy servant, who hath turned unto Thee in humility and submission and repentance, with the hosts of power and might and the armies of glory and dominion against every aggressive doubter and sinner mentioned in the Book and every contemptible impostor from among the people of the veil.

order.why: Read the appeal for deliverance from hardship.
shortened: Glorify thyself on My behalf, then beseech God to bestow upon us that which He hath bestowed upon thee and to deliver us from the world and its hardships and torments.

order.why: Ask for ease and an expanded heart.
Consider guidance along a straight path.
shortened: O Lord! Straighten for them the Path, appoint for them the guide which shall lead them to the door of Thy Inexhaustible Mercy, facilitate for them their affairs and shower upon them Thy heavenly Grace.

order.why: Hear the prayer that another person’s hopes may be fulfilled.
shortened: O Lord! Answer his prayer, facilitate his affairs, and perfect his joy through the attainment of his hopes.

order.why: Read the opening of the door of generosity.
Join that opening with what will truly benefit the petitioner.
Allow the urgency of an immediate need to be heard.
shortened: O God! By their right in Thy Book and their station in Thy knowledge, I beseech Thee to bless them with all Thy revelations, breezes, manifestations and stations which know no cessation, and to fulfill this need of mine now, now, now!

order.why: Read the invocations through sacred figures and names.
Consider refuge and supplication through Muhammad and his kindred.
Join gratitude for guidance with a prayer through the prophets.
shortened: Remember God's favor to you, then give thanks to Him and say:

"Praise be to Thee, O my God, for having created me and manifested me and guided me to Thy straight path. I beseech Thee by Thy Prophets and the Seal of Thy Messengers to assist me in that which Thou lovest and art pleased with.

order.why: Read the invocation through Him Who conversed upon Sinai.
shortened: I beseech Thee by Him Who conversed upon Sinai, through Whom the trumpet was sounded and the resurrection appeared, to assist Thy loved ones and Thy chosen ones to accomplish that which Thou hast commanded them in Thy Book.

order.why: Make prayer on behalf of many explicit.
Consider a community remembering and praying for one person.
Hear affection joined to intercession.
Extend the prayer to assistance in all conditions.
Include what benefits others in this world and the next.
shortened: We beseech God to assist all to serve Him and obey Him, and to ordain for His loved ones that which shall profit them in this world and the next.

order.why: Read the petition for the loved ones collectively.
